title: Finding Her Feet
subtitle: Maya's first job in a new country.
paras: By her second year abroad, Maya was ready to look for a part-time job. She spotted an advert for an internship at a small business in the city centre and filled in a lengthy questionnaire before being invited to an interview. Throughout it, she was conscious of every word she chose, careful not to exaggerate her experience. To her relief, the manager was friendly, and by the following Wednesday the job was hers.

The office was warm and comfortable, although the heating was so strong that the temperature made her drowsy after lunch. Her main task was the maintenance of the company calendar — booking meetings, chasing replies and making sure that double-booking never became a regular occurrence. She kept every receipt from work trips, since the company offered a guarantee that all costs would be repaid, and she soon learned to be thorough with the paperwork.

Maya occasionally joined her team for lunch at a little restaurant round the corner. She became close to a friendly neighbour from the next office, whose ancient vehicle broke down almost every week. There was the odd argument about whose turn it was to make the coffee, but nothing serious. On quiet afternoons she would slip up to the company library to read about the development of the industry she was now part of.

When the internship came to an end, Maya was determined not to disappoint the people who had taught her so much. She wrote a card to the committee that had hired her, signing it "Yours sincerely", and promised to come back the following summer. "See you tomorrow," her manager joked on her final morning — and somehow Maya sensed that her career had only just begun.
discuss: What did Maya gain from her first job, apart from the work itself? What makes a workplace somewhere people want to stay?

items.trick: BUSY changes its Y to I: busi + NESS.

items.trick: Double N, and it ends in -AIRE, like a French word.

items.clue: awake and aware of what is happening
items.trick: CON + SCIOUS: the SC is there, as in SCIence.

items.clue: to make something sound bigger or better than it is
items.trick: People exaggerate, so the word doubles its G.

items.clue: the day in the middle of the working week
items.trick: Capital W, and say it in your head as WED-NES-DAY.

items.clue: pleasant and relaxing to be in or wear
items.trick: COMFORT + ABLE: a FORT can be comfortable.

items.clue: how hot or cold something is
items.trick: Say every part: tem-PER-a-ture.

items.trick: Double C, double R, then -ENCE.

items.trick: E before I after C, and a silent P.

speaking: Talk about your first job, first day or first week somewhere new — real or imagined. Use at least six of the words. For two of them, spell the word out loud, part by part: "ques – tion – naire".
